# An upper bound of a sum, for radii

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `radd` · proved for finite operands · proved for infinite and NaN operands · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An upper bound of $a + b$, a number of `T`:

$$r \ge a + b.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of [`radd_entry`](radd_entry.md).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $a \ge 0$.
- $b \ge 0$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $r \ge a + b$, and $r - (a + b) \le \tfrac{3}{2}\,(r - \mathrm{pred}(r))$: at most $\tfrac{3}{2}$ gaps of the format above the exact value.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `radd_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Directed.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Directed.v), against `radd_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions radd_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition radd_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a b : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  fmt emin prec b ->
  0 <= a ->
  0 <= b ->
  let r := radd emin prec tie_even a b in
  fmt emin prec r /\
  (a + b) <= r /\ r - (a + b) <= (3 / 2) * (r - pred radix2 (FLT_exp emin prec) r).
```

## Infinite and NaN operands

The statement above is about finite operands. The claims also say what the kernel returns when its operands may be infinite or NaN. That statement requires:

- $a \ge 0$, or $+\infty$, or a NaN.
- $b \ge 0$, or $+\infty$, or a NaN.

and then:

- $r$ is a NaN exactly when an operand is a NaN.
- Otherwise $r \ge a + b$ (so $r = +\infty$ when an operand is $+\infty$), and when $r$ is finite it exceeds $a + b$ by at most $\tfrac{3}{2}$ gaps of the format.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

**Status of this statement:** proved. Rocq checks the theorem `radd_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeExt.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeExt.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions radd_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proofs of `radd_correct` and `radd_ieee_correct` depend on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** one step up from the rounded sum (Milestone 1 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/radd.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/radd.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# An upper bound of a + b, for radii: the rounded sum, one step up. For nonnegative operands it
# exceeds the exact sum by at most 3/2 gaps, which is sharp (a sum halfway between two numbers of
# the format that rounds up). For operands of any sign exhaustive runs give 2; not claimed.

s = add(a, b)
r = succ(s)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#radd)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest excess, in gaps | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 117 600 000 | 0 | 1.5 | yes |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 117 600 000 | 0 | 1.5 | yes |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 10 710 912 | 0 | 1.5 (`fp:8:-16:3`) | yes |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements of the statement on infinite and NaN operands.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
